sup:DEMO-F1.text:
Guten Tag,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below.

It is always a pleasure to work with your esteemed house, continuing the strong tradition of craftsmanship and trust between our companies. For this agreement, our offer stands at a price of €52.90 per unit, a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, valid from 1 December 2026. 

To remain transparent about our situation, WAGES-METAL rose 3.1 % in twelve months and is 28 % of our cost. We take great pride in the dedication of our foundry workforce and the quality we deliver to our partners every day.

Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days. We look forward to continuing our successful cooperation together.

Viele Grüße aus der Gießerei
Andreas Moser
Owner, Demo Gießerei GmbH

move.subject: Re: Quote from Demo Gießerei GmbH: Pump housing PH-100: the foundry wants +8.8 %
move.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining your position.
Thank you for your letter and for many years of reliable castings for the pump housing. We value you as a strategic partner and want a solution that keeps your business healthy. We have looked closely at energy and wage developments and believe they support a smaller adjustment, which we would like to pair with a longer commitment covering our full need.

Please find our proposal below.

We look forward to your reply.

Kind regards
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

move.text:
Guten Tag,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows. 

Our family foundry deeply values our long-standing partnership, and I gladly accept your proposal for a 24-month contract to ensure mutual stability for both of our companies. Our current offer stands at a price of €51.60 per unit, Zahlungsziel 60 days net, a contract term of 24 months, valid from 1 December 2026. 

In exchange for this extended commitment and our price concession, we must return to our standard 30-day payment terms. Alternatively, with Zahlungsziel 30 days net: a price of €51.30 per unit, Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 24 months, valid from 1 December 2026. 

You mentioned energy and wage developments; please provide the specific data you are referencing so we may review it. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

Viele Grüße aus der Gießerei
Andreas Moser
Owner, Demo Gießerei GmbH

decisions.why: within half a percent of our offer; C 413,600 below the limit 448,811

key_points: Single source for twelve years and a stabilise category: no alternative (fallback EUR 55 vs current 48.6), so the plan is moderate, argument-based pressure with no threats and no bluffs.

Their stated drivers are energy and wages. Market context cuts against energy (industrial power -43 % vs 2022) and puts wages at only +2.7 % and iron castings at +1.8 % y/y. These justify far less than +8.8 %, but they are context, not supplier-specific records.

Evidence is thin: no dossier and only market context arguments. The case refs (cost:part:PH-100, framework contract, scorecards, POs) exist but are not in our argument list. Do not quote figures we cannot check.
Key trades: 24 months as an explicit trade for price, and a later effective date tested in alternative sheets. Payment is held at 60 unless they ask; 45 is a possible closing trade.
Do not push below a healthy margin (4 %): the margin charge caps the benefit, so land near their full cost.
plan.stance_why: Strategic single source with no alternative and a margin charge below 4 %. Open moderately below their ask with term moves toward them rather than a hard anchor.

levers.why: Directly counters their energy driver; power prices are far below the crisis peak.

argument.note: 2026-09-12 market: Industrial power prices -43 % on 2022. Producer prices for electric power stand -43 % against August 2022. Do not cite it as about this supplier.

levers.why: Wages are only +2.7 % in manufacturing, so labour share times rise supports a small increase.

argument.note: 2026-09-20 market: Labour costs in manufacturing +2.7 %. Labour costs in German manufacturing rose +2.7 % year on year in the second quarter. Do not cite it as about this supplier.

levers.why: Iron castings producer prices are only +1.8 % y/y; a fresh fact for round two showing the market level of increase for their own product.

argument.note: 2026-09-14 market: Iron castings +1.8 % year on year. Producer prices for iron castings rose +1.8 % in the twelve months to August. Do not cite it as about this supplier.

trades.why: A two-year commitment covers our full need and is valued by suppliers.
The announced December start is their position. Offer it in one sheet at a lower price, and a later date in a second sheet.
Second sheet: January start at a slightly higher price, letting them choose and revealing their value of the months.
If they signal a cash need, 45 days costs little interest and can buy a price step at closing.

sup:DEMO-F1.opening_paragraph: Thank you for your letter and for many years of reliable castings for the pump housing. We value you as a strategic partner and want a solution that keeps your business healthy. We have looked closely at energy and wage developments and believe they support a smaller adjustment, which we would like to pair with a longer commitment covering our full need.
watch_for: Claims like 'energy rose X % and is Y % of our cost': respond with the power price context and share-times-rise arithmetic.
Requests for faster payment or binding volume: trade them only for price.
A declared final offer: accept it, or take their cheaper alternative sheet, if it is below fallback.
Insistence on the December date or an index clause request.
Signs of financial fragility, which argue for landing near their full cost.

risks: Thin evidence: market context may be dismissed as not specific to them. There is no supplier dossier.
No alternative: they may sense dependence, so avoid any signal of urgency.
Pushing too hard risks the margin charge and the relationship with a sole-source supplier.
Energy may be hedged at higher prices, which would make them reject the power price argument.
